kept.claim: The light-theme colour of the post-meta username link (.topic-meta-data h5 a) changes from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70%, making it much lighter on the default theme, and the dark-theme value (30%) is not the mirror of the original.
kept.evidence: The diff at desktop/topic-post.scss:291 changes the username link from 30% to dark-light-choose(70%, secondary 30%). dark-light-choose (variables.scss:46-52) returns the first argument on light themes, and the default $primary is #222 (colors.scss:1), so the link goes from about #646464 to about #bdbdbd (roughly 1.9:1 contrast on white). Every other converted line in the file keeps the original percentage as the first argument and uses 100-x for $secondary (lines 81, 113, 126, 278, 294).

kept.claim: The light-theme colour of .custom-message-length in the mobile flag modal changes from scale-color($primary, 70%) to 30%, making the helper text much darker, and the dark-theme argument (70%) is the inverse of the intended mirror.
kept.evidence: The diff at mobile/modal.scss:102 changes 70% to dark-light-choose(30%, secondary 70%), so the light-theme hint text goes from about #bdbdbd to about #646464. The desktop counterpart, desktop/modal.scss:92-94, uses (70%, 30%), which confirms the mobile percentages are swapped.

kept.claim: The mobile topic-map h3 light-theme colour changes from scale-color($primary, 20%) to 50%, making it the same colour as the h4 below it (also 50%) and removing the heading/sub-heading contrast.
kept.evidence: The diff at mobile/topic-post.scss:179-190 changes the topic-map h3 from 20% to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), the same as h4 at line 190. dark-light-choose returns its first argument on light themes, so h3 goes from about #4e4e4e to #919191. Other lines in the same file keep the original percentage (247: 20/80, 270: 75/25, 498: 70/30). The desktop lines the draft cited are not the h3 rule itself; the draft was corrected to cite lines in the same file.

kept.claim: The group-member .name light-theme colour changes from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 50% (in both desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497), so .name and .title now render the same grey and the name loses its emphasis.
kept.evidence: The diff at desktop/user.scss:519-528 and mobile/user.scss:494-504 changes .name from 30% to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), the same as .title (desktop :527, mobile :503). The light-theme output changes, and on dark themes .name gets secondary 50% instead of the 70% mirror.
